object_description: refined elongated volume with cut-outs and broken-line roof
design_condition: The building occupies the eastern half of the plot and frees the west for the playground, but its orientation and entrance turn the school’s back toward the village.

positive.statement: The volume is seductive at first glance, refined by its cut-outs and broken-line roof.
The typological proposal is interesting, with classrooms arranged around an elongated central hall.
The first-stage plan permits economical expansion by two or four classrooms without changing the basic typological principle or sloping roof.
The prefabricated construction is economical and quick, and the materiality is convincing.

negative.statement: The orientation of the project, particularly the position of the entrance, is questionable because the school turns its back on the village.
The exterior fittings are lacking in quality, with narrow access from the village and an injudicious location of vehicles beside and within the playground.
The hall remains the same size from one expansion stage to the next, which limits the typological proposal.
The desired big-house appearance seems incompatible with the character of a representative building.
The exceptional west facade does not correspond to the floor plan, and the positioning of the windows lacks precision.
The project is above average economically, with substantially more surface area and volume.
